q: Can foreigners buy property in the UAE?
a: Yes. Foreign nationals can buy freehold property in designated areas, which include most of the communities investors look at in Dubai (Downtown, Dubai Marina, JVC, Dubai Hills and many more) and investment zones in Abu Dhabi such as Al Reem, Saadiyat and Yas Island. You do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

q: Do I need to be in the UAE to buy?
a: No. Many buyers complete the whole purchase from abroad. Off-plan bookings can usually be signed digitally, and for ready property you can appoint someone with a power of attorney or use the developer's or trustee's remote signing options. You will need a valid passport copy and, for some steps, an Emirates ID or entry stamp.

q: What fees do I pay on top of the price?
a: In Dubai, the main ones are the 4% Dubai Land Department transfer fee, the registration trustee fee, and usually 2% + VAT agent commission on a resale. With a mortgage, add mortgage registration (0.25% of the loan), valuation and the bank's arrangement fee. On a typical AED 2M resale with a mortgage, fees come to roughly 7–8% of the price. Our true-cost calculator works it out for your numbers.

Dubai has one of the strongest off-plan protection systems in the region. Developers must be registered, the project must have its own escrow account at an approved bank, and buyers' payments are released only as construction progresses. Your job is to check the project in the Dubai REST app, pay only into the registered escrow account, and make sure your purchase is registered (Oqood). Our safety check walks you through the ten checks.

q: What is a post-handover payment plan?
a: A plan where part of the price is paid in instalments after you receive the keys, often over two to five years. It lowers the cash you need before handover, and if you rent the unit out, the rent can help cover the remaining instalments.

q: Can I sell an off-plan property before handover?
a: Often yes, but each developer sets its own rules. Many require a minimum percentage to be paid (commonly 30–40%) before they issue the no-objection certificate needed to transfer the unit. Check the resale clause in your Sale and Purchase Agreement before you book.

q: Can I get a mortgage as a non-resident?
a: Yes, several UAE banks lend to non-residents, usually with a larger deposit (often 40–50%) and stricter income checks. Residents buying a first home under AED 5M can often borrow up to 80%. Off-plan homes are usually financed only near or after handover, so most off-plan buyers pay through the developer's plan first.

q: What rental yield can I expect?
a: It depends heavily on the area, the building's service charge and the unit. Gross yields in popular Dubai apartment communities have often been in the 6–8% range, but net yield after service charges, empty weeks and management is lower. Use our rental yield calculator with the real service charge for the building.

q: Do I get a visa if I buy property?
a: Property worth at least AED 2 million can make you eligible for the UAE's 10-year, renewable Golden Visa, and mortgaged and off-plan property can count with conditions. Smaller investments may qualify for a shorter investor visa. See our Golden Visa page and always confirm the current rules with the authorities.
